\begin{tablenotes}[flushleft]
\footnotesize
\item \textit{Notes:} The sign strategy $q_t = \sign(\hat\sigma^2_t - \mathrm{IV}^2_t)$ on the \rheSzDays{} post-warmup days of $\mathcal T_{\mathrm{opt}}$; the short straddle holds $q_t \equiv -1$. $\SR$ is the annualized Sharpe ratio of Section~\ref{sec:rh_econ_measures}, at mid-quotes and at quoted bid/ask prices; mean return is the mean daily return in percent of the premium. Every comparison is at mid-quotes. $\Delta\SR$ is the difference of the Sharpe ratios: against the short straddle; against the same model class on the HAR benchmark set (full-set rows only); against the closing-interval HAR forecast (note c). Under each $\Delta\SR$, in brackets, the $p$-value of the paired block-bootstrap test of equal Sharpe ratios (block length \rheBootBlock{}, \rheBootN{} resamples); $t(\bar\Delta)$ is the $t$-statistic of the mean daily return differential against the short straddle (Newey--West, bandwidth $S = \rheHACS$, fixed-$b$ critical values; Section~\ref{sec:rh_methods_tests}). $^{*}$, $^{**}$ and $^{***}$ denote significance at the 10\%, 5\% and 1\% levels.
\item[a] Panels A and B: models estimated on the \rhePoolNBars{} regular-hours 30-minute intervals of each day (the pooled intraday scheme); each trades its 15:30 forecast of the 15:30--16:00 ET variance.
\item[b] On the HAR benchmark set the ridge, lasso and elastic net forecasts coincide with one another and with the pooled OLS (largest relative difference \rhemHarLinMaxRelDiff{} over \rhemHarLinNRows{} forecasts; the positions agree on every day), so Panel B holds \rhemHarDistinctWord{} distinct forecasts.
\item[c] The OLS on the HAR benchmark set estimated on the closing interval only (one observation a day), the HAR benchmark of Section~\ref{sec:rh_results}.
\end{tablenotes}
